coverage_note: Sections VI and XI, where omnitemporality and the Living Present carry the argument. Sections III, V, VII and X, which also carry term hits, are not extracted.

units.claim: Supratemporality and timelessness are said to be defined negatively only relative to mundane temporality; once that is reduced they appear as omnitemporality, a concrete mode of temporality in general.
units.quote: *Überzeitlichkeit* and *Zeitlosigkeit* are defined in their transcendence or negativity *only relative to mundane temporality*; once the latter is reduced, they appear as *Allzeitlichkeit* — omnitemporality, "*a concrete mode of temporality in general*."

units.claim: Supratemporality is denied to be an escape from time and called time's own universal mode, on the same reversal by which linguistic embodiment delivers rather than imprisons ideality.
units.quote: Supratemporality is thus not an escape from time but time's own universal mode — just as linguistic embodiment is not ideality's prison but its deliverance.

units.claim: The eternity of the Idea and of Reason is redefined as a historicity, its supra-temporality with regard to empirical temporality being nothing but an omnitemporality.
units.quote: But this eternity *is nothing but a historicity*. It is the possibility of history itself. Its *supra-temporality* — with regard to empirical temporality — *is nothing but an omnitemporality*.

units.claim: Primordial temporalization is called dialectical through and through, as the dialectic of the mutual implication of protentions and retentions with the non-dialectic identity of the Living Present.
units.quote: it was only the *dialectic of the dialectic* — the indefinite, mutual and irreducible implication of protentions and retentions — *with the non-dialectic*: the absolute and concrete identity of the Living Present, universal form of all consciousness.

units.claim: The coincidence of constituting and constituted moment is reread as a unity of non-coincidence and indefinite co-implication in a Living Present that projects and maintains itself dialectically.
units.quote: the unity of the *non-coincidence* and the *indefinite co-implication* of the constituted moment and the constituting moment, in the absolute identity of a Living Present that *projects and maintains itself dialectically*.

units.claim: Supra-temporality and omni-temporality are asked to be characters of Time itself, of the Living Present as the absolute concrete form of phenomenological temporality.
units.quote: Are not supra-temporality and omni-temporality *also the characters of Time itself*? — of the *Living Present*, which is the absolute concrete *Form* of phenomenological temporality and the primordial Absolute of all transcendental life?

units.claim: The hidden temporal unity of supra-temporality and omni-temporality is declared the unitary foundation of all the instances the reductions dissociated, and that unity is historicity itself.
units.quote: This unity — "as *temporal* unity of temporality, for every *Geschehen*, for all *history* as the *gathering of what comes to pass in general*" — "*is historicity itself*."

units.claim: Intentionality, traditionality, temporalization and historicity are said to be four names for one absolute movement, temporalization being the self-othering of the Living Present.
units.quote: traditionality (the transmission of sense), temporalization (the self-othering of the Living Present), and historicity are four names for one absolute movement

units.claim: The radical reduction is said to reach absolute transcendental subjectivity as pure passive-active temporality, the pure auto-temporalization of the Living Present, already intersubjective.
units.quote: *absolute transcendental subjectivity as pure passive-active temporality*, as the *pure auto-temporalization of the Living Present*

units.claim: The Living Present is disclosed as non-self-identical at its core, present only in deferring itself without respite, and this is named as the source of the structural delay of reflection.
units.quote: the *impotence to enclose oneself in the innocent indivision of the originary Absolute, because it is Present only in deferring itself without respite* (*en se différant sans relâche*)

units.claim: The self-differing of the Living Present through retention and protention is identified as différance in all but the later spelling, and Difference is called the opening through which presence is possible.
units.quote: it is "present" only by *differing from itself* — retention and protention (¶235), the going-out-from-self-into-self (¶261), now named as *différance* in all but the later spelling.
